scope: Static review of archived modified SwiftKey Beta 9.13.16.4 native smali; no Android device execution
hook: Lfc0/h;->invoke(Ljava/lang/Object;)Ljava/lang/Object; tail on each return, discriminator a == 0
discriminator_0: Dedicated emoji key: fc0.s1.g or the dedicated branch of fb0.g1.a
discriminator_1: Combined microphone/emoji key: action graph left unchanged; restores original toolbar access
timer: fc0.k1.w is copied from native fb0.r1.m(); hc0.k.a owns the timeout and oc0.p schedules it
long_press: androidx.fragment.app.u.run case 3 marks oc0.p.d=true BEFORE invoking hc0.k.b actors; original CLICK delegate oc0.b.c refuses when LONGPRESS is active
cancellation: oc0.p.b clears long-press/long-click flags and cancels its Runnable; oc0.p.k removes pending callback on slide-out; no external timer is introduced
fallback: LongPress stores only fallbackOnRelease boolean if toolbar cannot toggle. oc0.p.c only dispatches hc0.k.d on valid held release. Successful toggle needs no fallback.

short_action_routes.ordinary: fc0.h discriminator0 with fz.h.b()==false puts one ic0.a0 feature-opening actor into hc0.b.d (via builder.i). Native click path hc0.a.l invokes only this list.
short_action_routes.accessibility_action: With fz.h.b()==true, fc0.h puts one direct ic0.a0 into hc0.b.a.f (via builder.f). oc0.m.e invokes hc0.a.e, which invokes a.f; it does not call UP or click delegates.
short_action_routes.accessibility_slide_in_release: In the accessibility factory branch, builder.e receives the one wrapped ic0.a0 via builder.y. Native oc0.v only arms on slide-in h(), while its d() clears its armed flag. It invokes builder.e on UP if no LONGCLICK occurred.
short_action_routes.no_duplicate_native_short_route: Normal branch has opening actor only in d. Accessibility direct action uses a.f separately from touch UP. Accessibility d only contains reset helper(s); opening actor is in e. Therefore a single native short route does not close toolbar and then reopen emoji through a second wrapped action.
